method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. claims.claim: ⚠️ **Torticollis after trauma: manage as cervical spine assessment.**
claims.source_text: If torticollis occurs in setting of trauma, manage as Cervical spine assessment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever, signs of infection or abnormal neurology → appropriate imaging** to establish a cause.
claims.source_text: If the child has signs of fever, infection or abnormal neurology, appropriate imaging should be performed to establish a cause
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children have muscular torticollis** and can be managed with simple analgesia.
claims.source_text: Most children will have a muscular torticollis and can be managed with simple analgesia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Torticollis is a non-specific sign.** Causes: muscle spasm (wry neck); trauma (fracture/dislocation, spinal haematoma); atlantoaxial rotary subluxation/fixation; infection of head and neck, spine, CNS or upper lobe of the chest; juvenile idiopathic arthritis; posterior fossa and bone tumours; dystonia (including drug reactions); ocular dysfunction; benign paroxysmal torticollis.
claims.source_text: Torticollis (twisted neck), is a non-specific sign with a large spectrum of aetiologies … Muscle spasm (wry neck) Trauma: fracture/dislocation, spinal haematoma Atlantoaxial rotary subluxation/fixation Infection: head and neck, spine, CNS or upper lobe chest Inflammation: juvenile idiopathic arthritis Neoplasm: CNS (posterior fossa) and bone tumours Dystonic syndromes (idiopathic spasmodic torticollis, drug reactions) Ocular dysfunction Benign paroxysmal torticollis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Uncomplicated acute torticollis should resolve within 7–10 days.** Ask about an awkward position (recent flight, new sleeping arrangement) and trauma.
claims.source_text: Time course: uncomplicated acute torticollis should resolve within 7-10 days … History of awkward position eg recent flight, different sleeping arrangement History of trauma
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ask about infection and neurology:** fever, increased drooling, sore throat, dysphagia; headache, strabismus, diplopia, photophobia, ataxia.
claims.source_text: Infective symptoms: fever (see Febrile child), increased drooling, sore throat, dysphagia Neurological symptoms: headache, strabismus, diplopia, photophobia, ataxia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about drugs that cause acute dystonic reactions**, e.g. metoclopramide.
claims.source_text: Medications associated with acute dystonic reactions e.g. metoclopramide
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine:** midline tenderness, neck palpation and active range of motion; neurological, eye, ENT (including dentition and nodes) and chest examination. ⚠️ **Deep pathology such as infection may have no external signs.**
claims.source_text: Midline tenderness, general neck palpation and attempt active ROM … Location of tenderness may assist with diagnosis, however deep pathology (eg infection) may have no external signs … Neurologic examination Ophthalmologic examination ENT examination including dentition and lymph nodes Chest examination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider cervical spine X-ray**, particularly for cervical spine tenderness, severe pain, **symptoms persisting ≥1 week**, or risk of atlantoaxial instability (e.g. Down, Morquio, Larsen, Marfan syndromes).
claims.source_text: Cervical Spine X-ray: particularly if there is cervical spine tenderness, severe pain, persistent symptoms (≥1 week) or the child has a risk of atlantoaxial instability (eg Down syndrome, Morquio syndrome, Larsen syndrome, Marfan syndrome)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CT of the neck and/or brain if:** neurological symptoms · severe pain not relieved by analgesia or relaxants · suspected bone anomaly or abnormal X-ray · **suspected retropharyngeal abscess.**
claims.source_text: CT neck and/or the brain if: associated neurological symptoms are present severe pain is not alleviated by analgesia or relaxants bone anomaly is suspected clinically or abnormal cervical xray there is suspicion of a retropharyngeal abscess
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult** general medicine, orthopaedics, ENT, ophthalmology or neurology, depending on presentation, to guide imaging.
claims.source_text: Depending on the presentation, consultation with, general medicine, orthopaedics, ENT, ophthalmology or neurology will help with decisions about imaging
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children: heat pack, massage and basic analgesia.** Diazepam can help in some cases of sternocleidomastoid spasm.
claims.source_text: For most children, heat pack, massage and basic analgesia is appropriate treatment … Diazepam can be effective with some cases of spasm of the sternocleidomastoid
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Otherwise treat the cause; stabilisation may be required.** Infection: appropriate antibiotics. ⚠️ **Refer to ENT if a retropharyngeal or parapharyngeal abscess is suspected.**
claims.source_text: Management depends on suspected cause Stabilisation may be required Infectious cause: appropriate antibiotic therapy … Refer to ENT if a retropharyngeal or parapharyngeal abscess is suspected
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Atlantoaxial rotatory fixation:** rest and a soft collar. **Injury or congenital bony cause:** refer to orthopaedics. **Dystonic reaction:** benztropine.
claims.source_text: Atlantoaxial rotatory fixation: rest, use of a soft collar Injury or congenital bony cause: refer to orthopaedics Dystonic reactions: benztropine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for trauma, suspected deep neck space infection, or unknown cause or prolonged symptoms.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Trauma cases Deep space infection of the neck suspected Cause unknown or prolonged symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer** when care is beyond the comfort level of the local provider.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Child requires care beyond the comfort level of the local provider
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** when nothing on history or examination needs further investigation and follow-up is arranged; **GP or paediatric follow-up is advisable** after an ED diagnosis of torticollis.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when No features present on history or examination requiring further investigation Appropriate follow up arranged: GP/paediatric follow up is advisable in children discharged from ED with a diagnosis of torticollis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acquired torticollis' (Last updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acquired_torticollis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
